title: Model Compound Vulcanization—Part II. Comparison of Accelerators
abstract: Abstract         The efficiency of each of 20 accelerators to convert sulfur into sulfidic products has been evaluated by Model Compound Vulcanization. The sulfidic products can be isolated and identified by gas-liquid chromatography. The sulfidic products can be separated into groups of mono-, di- and trisulfides, with several isomeric products within each group. This paper has reported on the analysis of such isomeric products which correspond to different types of sulfur crosslinks in natural rubber vulcanizates. The analysis of monosulfidic product yields and of the isomer distribution within the monosulfide group is sufficient to characterize an accelerator.
